prompt: Which claims about the three strategies are true? Select all that apply.

options.text: Pairwise comparison uses O(1) extra space but takes O(n^2) time in the worst case.
A hash set spends up to O(n) extra space to get expected O(n) time.
Sorting takes O(n log n) time, and sorting in place may mutate the input.
Sorting first guarantees O(n) total time because the adjacent scan is linear.
The hash-set strategy uses O(1) extra space regardless of the input size.

explanation: Pairwise comparison minimizes extra storage but can examine quadratically many pairs. A hash set uses linear extra space for expected linear time. Sorting costs O(n log n); an in-place sort may use less explicit storage than a set, but it can change the input.
